question: Which type of line is used to represent hidden edges or surfaces in a technical drawing, as per BIS SP 46-2003?
solution:
The correct answer is __Dashed thin line**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dashed thin line__ is used to represent hidden edges or surfaces.
 
• It complies with the BIS SP 46-2003 standard.
 
• This line type helps to indicate features that are not directly visible in the given view.
 
• Hidden lines are drawn short-dashed and evenly spaced.
 
• They play a crucial role in communicating technical details in engineering and architectural drawings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Continuous thin line:**

 
 
• Used for dimension lines, projection lines, leader lines, etc.
 
 
 
• **Chain thin line:**
 
 
• Represents center lines, lines of symmetry, trajectories, etc.
 
 
 
• **Continuous thick line:**
 
 
• Used for visible outlines and edges.
